resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Icelandic source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Icelandic pass identified 25 actionable formula, terminology, grammar, and technical-clarity defects across electrical, circuit, trigonometric, thermal, heat-flux, and wire-gauge content; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Icelandic human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The heating-power title used a less natural Icelandic compound.
evidence: The previous title was Hitaafl.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Hitunarafl.

findings.summary: The Joule example described power as joules per second without stating watts clearly.
evidence: The previous conclusion used 7,2 joule á sekúndu.
findings.resolution: Clarified the result as 7,2 W or 72 J in 10 seconds.

findings.summary: The constant-current heat-power bullet had awkward Icelandic word order.
evidence: The previous bullet used a literal doubling construction.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as doubling resistance doubles heating power.

findings.summary: The constant-voltage bullet used heat energy where heating power was intended.
evidence: The previous bullet ended with hitaorku.
findings.resolution: Changed it to hitunarafl and clarified the lower-resistance relationship.

findings.summary: The series-resistor conclusion used an inconsistent word for resistors.
evidence: The previous conclusion used mótstöðurnar after the source used viðnám.
findings.resolution: Aligned the conclusion with the technical term viðnám.

findings.summary: The series-cell description used an awkward phrase for ampere-hour capacity.
evidence: The previous bullet used afkastageta amperstunda in an unnatural construction.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the sentence with natural Icelandic wording for ampere-hour capacity.

findings.summary: The parallel-cell description used an overly literal translation of parallel connection.
evidence: The previous bullet used a less natural phrase for cells in parallel.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the standard Icelandic hliðtenging wording.

findings.summary: The limits paragraph used an ungrammatical phrase for omitted model behavior.
evidence: The previous paragraph said to include all behavior that had been omitted with incorrect case and agreement.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the paragraph with correct Icelandic grammar and a clear high-current warning.

findings.summary: The TCR power formula omitted spacing around division.
evidence: The previous expression was I = V/R.
findings.resolution: Restored I = V / R.

findings.summary: The TCR limitation paragraph used a literal first-degree phrase and imprecise temperature wording.
evidence: The previous paragraph ended with fyrstu gráðu mati.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with first-order and temperature-range terminology.

findings.summary: The inverse-sine formula localized protected triangle-side labels.
evidence: The previous expression used öfugt and undirstúka inside the formula.
findings.resolution: Restored θ = sin^-1(opposite / hypotenuse).

findings.summary: The inverse-cosine formula localized protected triangle-side labels.
evidence: The previous expression used aðliggjandi and undirstúka inside the formula.
findings.resolution: Restored θ = cos^-1(adjacent / hypotenuse).

findings.summary: The inverse-tangent formula localized protected triangle-side labels.
evidence: The previous expression used öfugt and aðliggjandi inside the formula.
findings.resolution: Restored θ = tan^-1(opposite / adjacent).

findings.summary: The trigonometry worked formula localized the opposite-side label.
evidence: The previous expression began with gagnstæða rather than the protected formula label.
findings.resolution: Restored opposite = 10 × sin(30°) = 5 cm.

findings.summary: The second trigonometry worked formula localized the adjacent-side label.
evidence: The previous expression began with aðliggjandi rather than the protected formula label.
findings.resolution: Restored adjacent = 10 × cos(30°) ≈ 8,66 cm.

findings.summary: The waveform glossary used the English loanword amplitude.
evidence: The previous bullet said amplitude in otherwise Icelandic text.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the Icelandic technical term sveifluvídd.

findings.summary: The kelvin/Celsius comparison lacked clear unit spacing and phrasing.
evidence: The previous bullet rendered 1°C without the standard space.
findings.resolution: Rephrased it as equal 1 K and 1 °C temperature differences.

findings.summary: The electrical-heating conclusion spelled out the validated seconds result.
evidence: The previous conclusion ended with 523 sekúndur rather than the protected 523 s notation.
findings.resolution: Changed it to approximately 523 s.

findings.summary: The phase-change paragraph used a literal phrase for phase and latent heat.
evidence: The previous paragraph referred to the material's state and hidden heat with less precise terminology.
findings.resolution: Aligned it with fasi efnisins and eðlisbundinn dulinn varmi.

findings.summary: The phase-change limitations used varmahitun instead of the term for convection.
evidence: The previous list used an inaccurate heat-heating term.
findings.resolution: Changed it to varmaburður and corrected agreement throughout the paragraph.

findings.summary: The heat-flux description used the general heat-flow term rather than heat-flux density.
evidence: The previous description used Varmaflæði without identifying the per-area quantity.
findings.resolution: Aligned the description with Varmaflæðisþéttleiki.

findings.summary: The heat-flux summary did not state the per-area relationship directly.
evidence: The previous summary used a literal area-unit phrase.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the rate of heat transfer per area unit.

findings.summary: The heat-flux definition called q'' heat flow rather than heat-flux density.
evidence: The previous bullet said q'' er hitaflæði.
findings.resolution: Defined q'' as varmaflæðisþéttleiki in W/m².

findings.summary: The wire-gauge comparison used an awkward phrase for stranded construction.
evidence: The previous paragraph used strandað smíði.
findings.resolution: Changed it to fjölþátta uppbygging.

findings.summary: The wire-resistance formula omitted spaces around division.
evidence: The previous expression was R = ρ × L/A.
findings.resolution: Restored R = ρ × L / A.
